'''''Brute Force: Cracking the Data Encryption Standard''''' (2005, Copernicus Books {{ISBN|0387271600}}) is a book by [[Matt Curtin]] about [[cryptography]].

In this book, Curtin recounts his involvement in the [[DESCHALL Project]], mobilizing thousands of personal computers in 1997 in order to meet the challenge to crack a single message [[encryption|encrypted]] with [[Data Encryption Standard|DES]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Brute Force: Cracking the Data Encryption Standard |url=https://www.rsaconference.com/library/blog/brute-force-cracking-the-data-encryption-standard |access-date=January 20, 2024 |work=www.rsaconference.com}}</ref>

This was and remains one of the largest [[collaboration]]s of any kind on a single project in history.

The message was unencrypted on June 18 and was found to be "Strong cryptography makes the world a safer place."

This is also the message of Curtin's book where he uses a personal account to reveal to the uninitiated reader some insight into a topic of growing importance which is both technically and politically complicated.
